xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5361: bare-host-linux idle check fails ~3% of runs: pid-net counts machine-wide runner bursts that one 30 s baseline cannot cancel

plan.title: bare-host-linux idle check fails ~3% of runs: pid-net counts machine-wide runner bursts that one 30 s baseline cannot cancel
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The bare-host-linux idle check (pid-net) subtracts one 30 s baseline sample of machine-wide PID consumption from one 30 s idle sample. The kernel PID counter counts every process and thread on the runner, and the hosted runner produces random bursts of about +20 and +60 PIDs in about 5-7% of windows on both sides. A burst in the idle window fails the check (7 failures in 211 runs, all with the standard 6 traced Overdeck calls); a burst in the baseline window drives the net negative and would hide a real regression of up to about 60 PIDs.
narratives.Proposal: On Linux take 3 back-to-back baseline windows and 3 idle windows and decide pid-net on min(idle) - min(baseline), so one burst in any one window cannot move the verdict. macOS keeps exactly one window per side and its traced-cost rule. Move the verdict program out of the inline node -e into scripts/bare-host-smoke/result.mjs with pure exports and a unit test. Record the dashboard tree's process and task counts from /proc at window boundaries with bash builtins only, and print a heuristic excess-source attribution on a Linux failure. Add --idle-spawner-ms and a gated bare-host-linux-spawner-canary CI job as the positive control. Calibrate the Linux budget with the D14 rule on 20+ runs from a temporary push-triggered workflow that is deleted before done. Update the script comments, RELEASING.md, PIPELINE-GATES.md and conventions.md. Full detail: .pan/drafts/pan-5361.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Changing the macOS measure, window count, timing, budget or traced-cost formula.
- Changing any Overdeck idle behaviour (pollers, CLIProxy download, systemd helpers).
- Raising IDLE_BUDGET_LINUX above 30.
- Exact per-process PID attribution via PID namespaces, cgroups, eBPF or process accounting.
- Catching idle work whose period is longer than one 30 s window; min-of-N can miss it (accepted limit).
- Naming the runner process behind the bursts.
- Leaving the temporary calibration workflow or a matrix on bare-host-linux in the final diff.
- A changelog.d entry (CI-only change).

autoDecisions.summary: Estimator is min(idle) - min(baseline) over 3 windows per side on Linux.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names it as its first option; a steady regression shows in every idle window so the minimum keeps it, while min-of-3 survives up to two bursts per side.

autoDecisions.summary: macOS stays at one window per side with today's stamps.
autoDecisions.rationale: AC5 requires the macOS traced-cost rule unchanged and the known-bad job reads its fields; extra macOS windows would only cost queue time.

autoDecisions.summary: The spawner canary uses 500 ms, not the issue's 2 s example.
autoDecisions.rationale: 2 s adds about +15 per window, giving a net of about 21, which passes the budget of 30 under both the old and new measure; 500 ms adds about +60 and fails clearly.

autoDecisions.summary: The controlled run is a permanent --idle-spawner-ms flag plus a CI job gated on smoke changes.
autoDecisions.rationale: The smoke cannot run on a host with a live dashboard (port guard), so evidence must come from CI; a permanent gated canary mirrors bare-host-macos-known-bad and keeps proving the estimator catches steady spawners.

autoDecisions.summary: Calibration runs on a temporary push-triggered workflow smoking @overdeck/core@0.86.0, deleted before done.
autoDecisions.rationale: ci.yml runs only on PRs and main with cancel-in-progress concurrency, and workflow_dispatch needs the file on main; the published package has the same idle profile and needs no build.

autoDecisions.summary: Linux budget is recalculated with the D14 rule from the 20 calibration nets; fallback N=5 if any run bursts in every window of one side.
autoDecisions.rationale: D14 is the documented calibration rule; later idle windows are uncharted, so an explicit stop rule guards the choice of N.

autoDecisions.summary: Attribution is a heuristic: shell calls weigh 2, plus tree task growth; source is dashboard-tree when 2 x attributed >= excess.
autoDecisions.rationale: /proc has no per-process fork counter; weighting shell calls as an upper bound biases toward blaming the dashboard, the safer side.

metadata.acJustification: Six criteria: the estimator, its failure case, the frozen macOS path, attribution, the shell wiring and the no-window failure path are separate behaviours a reviewer checks separately.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-1. Add SCRIPT_DIR after set -u. Create scripts/bare-host-smoke/result.mjs (ESM, isMain guard like scripts/windows-smoke/summarize.mjs) exporting summarizeSpawns, decideIdle, renderLines and renderStepSummary, ported from the inline node -e program at scripts/bare-host-smoke.sh:174-270 plus the min-of-N estimator, per-window fields and the FR-6 attribution. Replace the node -e body of write_result with node "$SCRIPT_DIR/bare-host-smoke/result.mjs" using the PRD env contract, and shim the single-window values into R_BASELINE_WINDOWS/R_IDLE_WINDOWS/R_IDLE_FROM/R_IDLE_TO in measure_idle until multi-window-measure lands. Write tests/unit/scripts/bare-host-smoke-result.test.ts with the named tests in the PRD. When there are no idle windows, spawns, idleNew, net, value and attribution are null, pass is false and result.json is still written.

items.title: Given baseline windows [7, 72, 6] and idle windows [13, 12, 14] on linux, decideIdle returns net 6 and pass true at budget 30; given idle [13, 77, 12] with baseline [7, 8, 6] it also returns net 6

Keep every construct bash 3.2 compatible.

Snapshot the dashboard tree's procs and tasks from /proc at Linux idle window boundaries

expected_outputs: the awk/grep count prints 0 (no forks in tree_snapshot)

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-3. Add tree_snapshot <root_pid> that sets TREE_PROCS and TREE_TASKS from /proc/[0-9]*/stat (ppid field 4, num_threads field 20) and /proc/<pid>/cmdline matches of "$WORK_DIR/home/" or "$WORK_DIR/tools/", using only builtins and indexed arrays, then call it on Linux before the first idle window and after every idle window, outside the counter reads, appending procs:tasks to R_IDLE_TREE for result.mjs. Snapshots are per window, not shared: when a negative count forces a retake, take a fresh start snapshot immediately before the retake's from stamp and replace the old start; R_IDLE_TREE holds one startProcs:startTasks:endProcs:endTasks entry per window.

items.title: The tree_snapshot function body contains no command substitution, backtick or pipe, so it spawns no process

tree_snapshot is called only when OS_NAME is linux, before each idle window's from stamp and after its to stamp, and appends one startProcs:startTasks:endProcs:endTasks entry per window to R_IDLE_TREE
tree_snapshot counts the server pid, its ppid descendants and processes whose cmdline contains $WORK_DIR/home/ or $WORK_DIR/tools/; bash -n exits 0
When a negative count forces a retake, take_windows calls tree_snapshot again before the retake's from stamp and replaces that window's start snapshot

metadata.sizeJustification: Nine files, one feature: the subsystem count comes from directory spread (the smoke script, its new helper module, its test, two workflow files, the PRD evidence section and three doc files), not from separate concerns. Every item edits or depends on the one smoke script's measurement contract, so sibling issues could not ship or be verified on their own.
